title: Round 37 Connecticut-Rhode Island state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Connecticut and Rhode Island. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county (Connecticut: planning region), permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Bear Mountain and Jerimoth Hill carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The Connecticut River closure, the Mount Frissell slope problem, the Connecticut planning-region county equivalents, and the unseedable Candlewood Lake screen are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. Historical county records (Connecticut's abolished counties), adjacent harbour/reservoir records, census-designated places, and shoreline-community records were rejected explicitly where relevant. Note: for Connecticut the Geocoder county strings are the nine planning regions with their full 'Planning Region' suffix, while the DomesticNames county column stores the same regions without the suffix (e.g. Capitol); the stored county reproduces the extract value.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Bear Mountain (205348) and Jerimoth Hill (1219566), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the summit elevations cite USGS-published values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-19; this register is the frozen batch-19 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county (or Connecticut planning region), permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (text class Reservoir for Lake Lillinonah and Scituate Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit. Bay-class records (Narragansett Bay, the named harbours) are outside the seeded row classes and remain context corridors.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor (the Pawcatuck River under RI; Candlewood Lake's shoreline-community screen).
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

connecticut.title: Connecticut statewide frame (Connecticut-Rhode Island batch)
connecticut.frameNote: Connecticut-Rhode Island batch: the Hartford capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Bear Mountain summit check (2,323 ft), Bantam Lake and Lake Lillinonah, and three Long Island Sound river mouths. The Connecticut River seeds here on FEATURE_ID 206425, closing the corridor chain that ran through New Hampshire, Vermont, and Massachusetts (batches 17-18). County strings are the GNIS planning regions.

identityDecisions.candidate: Connecticut River FEATURE_ID 206425 (Streams & Canals, Lower Connecticut River Valley region)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded on its Connecticut mouth record. After reservoir-only screens under NH and VT (batch 17) and MA (batch 18), the main stem seeds at the fourth frame of the chain — the counterpart of the Mississippi (Minnesota to Louisiana), Pearl (Mississippi to Louisiana), Androscoggin/Saco/Merrimack (New Hampshire to Maine/Massachusetts) closures.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The stored point is the GNIS primary point, not a channel centerline.

identityDecisions.candidate: Mount Frissell under states=CT (empty screen) vs Bear Mountain FEATURE_ID 205348
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded Bear Mountain, the highest Connecticut summit (2,323 ft). Connecticut's highest ground is the Mount Frissell south slope (2,379 ft), but the Frissell summit record keys to Massachusetts and the CT screen returns an empty array, so no Connecticut record exists to seed for the slope. The Danbury-area Bear Mountain namesake (205347) is rejected by region, point, and elevation context.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Bear Mountain is not represented as the state high point — the register distinguishes highest summit from highest ground.

identityDecisions.candidate: Candlewood Lake Geocoder screen (shoreline communities only)
identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. Both the exact-name and bare-name screens return only Candlewood Isle/Knolls/Lake Club/Orchards/Pines/Point/Shores/Springs community and CDP records; no identity-safe lake record was returned, so the state's largest lake by area stays unseeded and Bantam Lake (largest natural lake) plus Lake Lillinonah carry the frame's lake rows.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: No community point is presented as the lake.

identityDecisions.candidate: Farmington River FEATURE_ID 207042 (valid Stream record, Capitol region)
identityDecisions.decision: Returned a valid, identity-safe record but is not seeded: the 12-row starter register prioritizes the three Sound-draining main stems (Connecticut, Housatonic, Thames). Recorded here so the omission is a visible selection, not a screening failure.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Absence from the gazetteer is not absence from GNIS.

identityDecisions.decision: Corridor-only in the Rhode Island frame. The Pawcatuck forms the RI/CT border; its RI-filtered screen returns an empty array, consistent with a Connecticut-keyed primary record. The Connecticut extract staging also screened the name under CT candidate lists without a seeded row being taken in either frame.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridor is not a channel centerline or state boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Connecticut county equivalents (planning regions) vs Rhode Island counties
identityDecisions.decision: Connecticut rows store the DomesticNames planning-region strings (Capitol, Northwest Hills, ...) because GNIS replaced the abolished county governments with the nine councils of governments; the Geocoder returns the same regions with the Planning Region suffix, preserved in each register row's geocoderCounty. Rhode Island keeps its five constitutional counties and stores County names normally.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Planning-region strings are GNIS county equivalents, not revived counties.

knownLimitations: Connecticut and Rhode Island are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Bear Mountain (2,323 feet) and Jerimoth Hill (812 feet) elevations cite USGS-published values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction. Connecticut's highest ground (Mount Frissell south slope, 2,379 feet) has no Connecticut GNIS record and is documented rather than seeded.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. The Connecticut rectangle includes Long Island Sound water and the Rhode Island rectangle reaches Block Island; no boundary geometry is claimed.
